     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveSpace
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Projective and H-quasi-projective morphisms
    10	
    11	This file supplies the universe-polymorphic geometric core of projectivity that
    12	Mathlib v4.31 does not yet provide. A morphism is projective when it factors as
    13	a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional relative projective space.
    14	
    15	A morphism is **H-quasi-projective** when it factors through a quasi-compact
    16	immersion into such a projective space, following the finite-projective-space
    17	convention of [Stacks, Tag 01VV].  The quasi-compactness is part of the
    18	definition: without it the predicate only records an immersion/relative very
    19	ampleness and need not imply finite type.  This predicate is not asserted to
    20	be equivalent over arbitrary bases to every formulation using relative ample
    21	line bundles.  Both predicates are stable under base change.
    22	
    23	The line-bundle-carrying refinement used by the Quot construction remains in
    24	`Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean`; that refinement is universe-monomorphic because
    25	its Serre twist is built by the project-local sheaf gluing engine.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory Limits
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	universe u
    33	
    34	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    35	
    36	/-- A morphism is projective if it admits a closed immersion into a
    37	finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    38	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    39	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    40	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    41	
    42	/-- A morphism is H-quasi-projective if it admits a quasi-compact immersion into
    43	a finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    44	def Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    45	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    46	    IsImmersion i ∧ QuasiCompact i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    47	
    48	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    49	
    50	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
    51	
    52	/-- A projective morphism is H-quasi-projective. -/
    53	theorem isHQuasiProjective (h : pi.IsProjective) : pi.IsHQuasiProjective := by
    54	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    55	  letI : Finite n := hn
    56	  haveI : IsClosedImmersion i := hi
    57	  exact ⟨n, hn, i, inferInstance, inferInstance, hcomp⟩
    58	
    59	/-- Projective morphisms are proper. -/
    60	theorem isProper (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsProper pi := by
    61	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    62	  letI : Finite n := hn
    63	  haveI := hi
    64	  rw [← hcomp]
    65	  infer_instance
    66	
    67	/-- Projective morphisms are locally of finite type. -/
    68	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : pi.IsProjective) : LocallyOfFiniteType pi :=
    69	  haveI := h.isProper
    70	  inferInstance
    71	
    72	/-- Projective morphisms are separated. -/
    73	theorem isSeparated (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsSeparated pi :=
    74	  haveI := h.isProper
    75	  inferInstance
    76	
    77	/-- Projective morphisms are universally closed. -/
    78	theorem universallyClosed (h : pi.IsProjective) : UniversallyClosed pi :=
    79	  haveI := h.isProper
    80	  inferInstance
    81	
    82	/-- A closed immersion into a projective scheme is projective. -/
    83	theorem comp_isClosedImmersion (h : pi.IsProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    84	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] : (j ≫ pi).IsProjective := by
    85	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    86	  letI : Finite n := hn
    87	  haveI := hi
    88	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩
    89	
    90	/-- The comparison morphism from the base-changed source to the corresponding
    91	base change of its ambient projective space. -/
    92	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
    93	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
    94	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
    95	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
    96	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
    97	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
    98	
    99	/-- Projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
   100	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
   101	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsProjective := by
   102	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
   103	  letI : Finite n := hn
   104	  haveI := hi
   105	  refine ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp, ?_, ?_⟩
   106	  · have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
   107	        pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   108	    have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst pi g)
   109	        (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
   110	      have hbig : IsPullback
   111	          (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
   112	          (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
   113	        rw [h1, hcomp]
   114	        exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
   115	      exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
   116	        (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
   117	        (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
   118	    exact MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi
   119	  · exact IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   120	
   121	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
   122	
   123	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective
   124	
   125	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
   126	
   127	/-- H-quasi-projective morphisms are locally of finite type. -/
   128	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) : LocallyOfFiniteType pi := by
   129	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, _, hcomp⟩ := h
   130	  letI : Finite n := hn
   131	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   132	  rw [← hcomp]
   133	  infer_instance
   134	
   135	/-- H-quasi-projective morphisms are quasi-compact. -/
   136	theorem quasiCompact (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) : QuasiCompact pi := by
   137	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hqc, hcomp⟩ := h
   138	  letI : Finite n := hn
   139	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   140	  haveI : QuasiCompact i := hqc
   141	  rw [← hcomp]
   142	  infer_instance
   143	
   144	/-- H-quasi-projective morphisms are separated. -/
   145	theorem isSeparated (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) : IsSeparated pi := by
   146	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, _, hcomp⟩ := h
   147	  letI : Finite n := hn
   148	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   149	  rw [← hcomp]
   150	  infer_instance
   151	
   152	/-- A quasi-compact immersion into an H-quasi-projective scheme is
   153	H-quasi-projective. -/
   154	theorem comp_isImmersion (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
   155	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j] :
   156	    (j ≫ pi).IsHQuasiProjective := by
   157	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hqc, hcomp⟩ := h
   158	  letI : Finite n := hn
   159	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   160	  haveI : QuasiCompact i := hqc
   161	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩
   162	
   163	/-- The comparison from a base-changed source to the corresponding base change
   164	of its ambient projective space. -/
   165	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
   166	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
   167	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
   168	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
   169	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
   170	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
   171	
   172	/-- H-quasi-projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
   173	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
   174	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsHQuasiProjective := by
   175	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hqc, hcomp⟩ := h
   176	  letI : Finite n := hn
   177	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   178	  haveI : QuasiCompact i := hqc
   179	  have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
   180	      pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   181	  have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst pi g)
   182	      (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
   183	    have hbig : IsPullback
   184	        (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
   185	        (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
   186	      rw [h1, hcomp]
   187	      exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
   188	    exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
   189	      (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
   190	      (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
   191	  exact ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp,
   192	    MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi,
   193	    MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hqc, h1⟩
   194	
   195	end Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective
   196	
   197	namespace ProjectiveSpace
   198	
   199	/-- The structural morphism of relative projective space is projective. -/
   200	theorem isProjective_over (n : Type u) [Finite n] (S : Scheme.{u}) :
   201	    (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S).IsProjective :=
   202	  ⟨n, inferInstance, 𝟙 _, inferInstance, Category.id_comp _⟩
   203	
   204	/-- The structural morphism of relative projective space is H-quasi-projective. -/
   205	theorem isHQuasiProjective_over (n : Type u) [Finite n] (S : Scheme.{u}) :
   206	    (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S).IsHQuasiProjective :=
   207	  (isProjective_over n S).isHQuasiProjective
   208	
   209	end ProjectiveSpace
   210	
   211	end AlgebraicGeometry

  1319	/-- **The identity component is of finite type and geometrically irreducible.**
  1320	
  1321	Kleiman §5 Lem.~`lem:agps`~(3) conclusion (c): the open subgroup `G^0` of
  1322	a `k`-group scheme `G` locally of finite type is itself
  1323	locally-of-finite-type-plus-quasi-compact (i.e., of finite type) over `k`,
  1324	and is geometrically irreducible. The proof reduces (after base change to
  1325	`\bar k`) to picking a nonempty irreducible open subset `U ⊆ G^0`; the
  1326	translates `zg⁻¹U` give an open cover of the closed points of `G^0` by
  1327	irreducible neighbourhoods, extended to all points by Jacobson density, so
  1328	with connectedness this gives irreducibility globally (EGA I 6.1.10). The
  1329	image `α(W × W) ⊆ G^0` of an affine open `W ∋ e` under the group law is
  1330	quasi-compact and contains all closed points, so finitely many affine opens
  1331	cover `G^0` and `G^0` is quasi-compact.
  1332	
  1333	The three conjuncts are obtained as follows: `LocallyOfFiniteType` because
  1334	the structural morphism is an open immersion composed with `G.hom`;
  1335	`QuasiCompact` from `identityComponent_compactSpace` (Kleiman's product trick
  1336	over the algebraic closure, Jacobson density, and descent along the
  1337	surjective base-change projection) together with the affine-target
  1338	characterisation of quasi-compactness; `GeometricallyIrreducible` from
  1339	`identityComponent_geometricallyIrreducible` (translation of an irreducible
  1340	open through all closed points over the algebraic closure, EGA I 6.1.10, and
  1341	descent along the surjective projection from the algebraic closure of each
  1342	field extension). -/

  1348	      QuasiCompact (IdentityComponent G).hom ∧
  1349	      GeometricallyIrreducible (IdentityComponent G).hom := by

  1357	/-! ## §2. The identity component of the Picard scheme
  1358	
  1359	We specialise the abstract identity-component substrate to
  1360	`G = PicScheme C`, the Picard scheme of a smooth proper geometrically
  1361	integral curve `C/k` (from sibling `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
  1362	
  1363	Blueprint reference: `def:pic_zero_subscheme` (Kleiman §5 opening + Prp.
  1364	`prp:pic0`). -/
  1365	
  1366	namespace Scheme
  1367	
  1368	/-- The **identity component of the Picard scheme** `Pic⁰_{C/k}`.
  1369	
  1370	Defined as the identity component
  1371	`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` of the Picard scheme
  1372	`Pic_{C/k}` (from sibling `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`,
  1373	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme`). By
  1374	`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme`, `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is an
  1375	open and closed subgroup scheme of `Pic_{C/k}` of finite type over `k`,
  1376	geometrically irreducible, and its formation commutes with extension of the
  1377	base field.
  1378	
  1379	The two instances required by the §1 substrate are available for
  1380	`PicScheme C`: the group structure `GrpObj (PicScheme C)` (by Yoneda
  1381	transport, `PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`) and local finiteness, carried by
  1382	`PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1)). Consequently
  1383	the §1 substrate theorems (`isOpenSubgroupScheme`,
  1384	`isSubgroupHomomorphism`, `identityComponent_geometricallyConnected`,
  1385	`baseChangeIso`) apply to `Pic⁰_{C/k}` definitionally. -/
  1386	noncomputable def Pic0Scheme {k : Type u} [Field k]
  1387	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
  1388	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  1389	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
  1390	    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :
  1391	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
  1392	  GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)
  1393	
  1394	/-! ## §3. The degree map
  1395	
  1396	The disjoint-union structure of `Pic_{C/k}` (a disjoint union of open
  1397	quasi-projective `k`-subschemes, indexed by Hilbert polynomial via
  1398	`PicScheme.smoothProperQuotient`) stratifies its `T`-points by the leading
  1399	coefficient of the Hilbert polynomial of a representing invertible sheaf
  1400	relative to a fixed degree-one polarisation. On `k`-points this gives the
  1401	**degree map** `Pic_{C/k}(k) → ℤ`.
  1402	
  1403	Blueprint reference: `def:divisor_degree_pic` (Milne III.1, p.~88). -/
  1404	
  1405	namespace PicScheme
  1406	
  1407	/-! ### The degree, factored through the relative Picard group
  1408	
  1409	The route below replaces the Quot/Hilbert-polynomial construction the section header
  1410	describes. Two facts make it work, and neither needs Quot:
  1411	
  1412	1. **Representability already does the transport.** `PicScheme.representable C` is a
  1413	   bijection `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` natural in `T`; taking
  1414	   `T = Spec k` (the trivial over-object `Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))`) sends a `k`-rational point
  1415	   of `Pic_{C/k}` to a relative Picard class over the base. This is `classOfSection` below,
  1416	   and it is sorry-free.
  1417	2. **The degree is a homomorphism on those classes.** ⚠ This was described here as "the one
  1418	   remaining input, isolated as the class `ClassDegree`". That is **false** and is corrected at
  1419	   `ClassDegree` below: the class is inhabited by the zero homomorphism with no hypothesis, so
  1420	   it demands nothing and `degreeOfSection` is not pinned to the degree. What is actually
  1421	   missing is a *characterisation* of the homomorphism. The sibling project builds exactly this
  1422	   homomorphism sorry-free and without Quot — `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`,
  1423	   `RiemannRoch/RelPicDegree.lean`, `relPicDeg : Additive (relPic C (overSpec k K)) →+ ℤ`,
  1424	   descended from `classDeg` along the observation that `Spec K` is a one-point space so its
  1425	   Čech Picard group is trivial and cannot contribute. Its own input is the closed χ-ledger
  1426	   `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg D` (`RiemannRoch/ChiLedger.lean`), whose 22-file / 5.5k-line
  1427	   closure I measured to be free of `sorry`.
  1428	
  1429	WHY `degree`'s DOMAIN IS AWKWARD — but *not* a reason it cannot be defined. `degree` takes an
  1430	*arbitrary* morphism `Spec k ⟶ (PicScheme C).left`, not a morphism over `Spec k`. Such a
  1431	morphism need not be a section of `(PicScheme C).hom` — the goal
  1432	`lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec k)` is not derivable — so it does not name a
  1433	`k`-*rational* point and representability says nothing about it.
  1434	
  1435	⚠ AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS PARAGRAPH DREW A FALSE CONCLUSION from that, and it is corrected
  1436	at `degree` (now closed, run 0067 r4) rather than only here. It read: "A total function of that
  1437	type therefore cannot be built from the Picard functor at all; it would have to invent a value
  1438	off the sections." Inventing a value off the sections is precisely what a total function of
  1439	this type is *allowed* to do — `fun _ => 0` inhabits the type — so the impossibility claim was
  1440	false, and the observation only ever constrained which values are **pinned**. `degree` is now
  1441	defined by cases on the section condition, agreeing with `degreeOfSectionPinned` where that is
  1442	meaningful; see `degree_eq_degreeOfSectionPinned`.
  1443	
  1444	Consumers should still prefer `degreeOfSection` / `degreeOfSectionPinned`, which carry the
  1445	section hypothesis in their types and so cannot be misread as speaking about non-sections. -/
  1446	
  1447	/-- An additive integer-valued function on relative Picard classes of `C` over the base field
  1448	— the carrier shape of Milne III.1 p.~88.
  1449	
  1450	**⚠ THIS CLASS IS VACUOUS AS STATED, and the docstring that used to sit here — "the one
  1451	remaining input to the degree map" — was FALSE.** Corrected run 0067 r2 after inbox issue
  1452	I-0534, re-verified by machine rather than accepted on report:
  1453	
  1454	```
  1455	theorem probe_classDegree_no_gate … : PicScheme.ClassDegree C := ⟨⟨0⟩⟩
  1456	-- axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]   -- no gate, no sorry
  1457	```
  1458	
  1459	The field asks only for `Nonempty (… →+ ℤ)`, and the **zero homomorphism** inhabits that type
  1460	with no hypothesis whatsoever. So `ClassDegree` is a *theorem* of this project, not an open
  1461	input, and nothing here demands that the chosen map be a degree.
  1462	
  1463	WHAT THAT COSTS THE CONSUMERS BELOW, stated plainly: `degreeOfSection` is total but **not
  1464	pinned to the degree** — `degreeOfSection ≡ 0` is a permitted reading of every statement in this
  1465	section — and `degreeOfSection_eq_zero_of_class_eq_zero` is correspondingly contentless (it is
  1466	`map_zero`, true of the zero map too). Do not cite them as a constructed degree map.
  1467	
  1468	THE REAL MISSING INPUT is a **characterisation**, not an existence claim: agreement of the
  1469	chosen homomorphism with `Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree` on the class of `𝒪(D)`, or with the
  1470	sibling's `relPicDeg` under the carrier comparison. That is what would make the class
  1471	non-vacuous and the degree unique. The class is retained (rather than deleted) only because
  1472	`degreeOfSection` is pinned against it; whoever adds the pinning field owns updating both.
  1473	
  1474	Contrast the house pattern: `HasPicScheme` and `HasFiniteMapToP1` are well *stated* because they
  1475	assert existence of an object satisfying a *nontrivial property*, where this one asks for a map
  1476	with no property — which is why it collapsed. But note the difference between a good statement
  1477	and an inhabited one (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-29): `HasFiniteMapToP1` has a derived instance,
  1478	whereas `HasPicScheme` has **zero** instances — its only producer, `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`,
  1479	is deliberately not an instance and needs `[HasRationalPoint C]`, which itself has no
  1480	unconditional producer since `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` was deleted as FALSE (`I-0491`). So
  1481	`HasPicScheme` is the right shape over an empty domain, and 70 declarations bind it. New work
  1482	belongs on `HasPicSchemeEt`/`picEt`. -/
  1483	class ClassDegree {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
  1484	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  1485	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : Prop where

     9	# Homogeneity of a group scheme: translations, and the invariants they move
    10	
    11	A group scheme is **homogeneous**: any point can be carried to any other by an automorphism
    12	of the underlying scheme, namely a translation. This file supplies the translation and the
    13	consequence the dimension chapter needs — that a *pointwise* invariant of the local rings is
    14	constant along the orbit of the translations, so a bound at one point is a bound at every
    15	point in that orbit.
    16	
    17	## Why this file exists
    18	
    19	`Picard/Pic0Dimension.lean` reduces `dim Pic⁰_{C/k} = g(C)` to two halves. The `≥` half
    20	needs the cotangent dimension at the **identity** only, and is front (a) of this chapter.
    21	The `≤` half is
    22	```
    23	∀ z, dim_{κ(z)} (m_z / m_z²) ≤ g
    24	```
    25	— a bound at *every* point
    26	(`Pic0.topologicalKrullDim_le_genus_of_forall_finrank_cotangentSpace_le`).
    27	The previous reading of that hypothesis was that it is a genuinely new *uniform* statement,
    28	different in kind from the one-point identity front (a) produces. On a **group** scheme that
    29	reading is too pessimistic, and this file records why: translations act transitively on the
    30	rational points, and they are isomorphisms of the underlying scheme, so the cotangent
    31	dimension is the same at any two points connected by one.
    32	
    33	What this does and does not buy, stated precisely because the distinction is the whole
    34	content:
    35	
    36	* it **does** turn the uniform hypothesis into a statement about *one* orbit representative
    37	  plus a transitivity statement about the points — `finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_of_pointTranslation`
    38	  is the transport, and it is unconditional;
    39	* it does **not** by itself discharge the uniform hypothesis, because the translations here are
    40	  indexed by *sections* `𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ G`, i.e. by `S`-rational points, and a scheme over a
    41	  non-closed field has points that are not rational. Over an algebraically closed field the
    42	  closed points are all rational and the orbit is the whole closed-point set; in general the
    43	  residue-field extension is the gap. So the honest statement of what remains is "every point
    44	  of `Pic⁰` is a translate of the identity", which is a statement about *points*, not about
    45	  dimension theory.
    46	
    47	That is a strictly better place for the residue than "a uniform cotangent bound", which is
    48	what the roadmap recorded before: it moves the open content out of dimension theory (where
    49	this project had to build `Picard/EmbeddingDimensionBound.lean` to make progress) and into
    50	the homogeneity of a group scheme, where the mathematics is standard.
    51	
    52	## Provenance
    53	
    54	`CategoryTheory.GrpObj.pointTranslation` and its scheme-level shadow are ported from the
    55	sibling project `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`,
    56	`AlgebraicJacobian/AbelianVariety/Translation.lean` (sorry-free there). The port is free:
    57	the general half is pure `CartesianMonoidalCategory` reasoning on top of mathlib's
    58	`CategoryTheory.GrpObj.mulRight` (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Grp.lean:275`) and needs
    59	no project-specific input at all. AJC had no `pointTranslation` of any kind before this file
    60	(grep: zero occurrences).
    61	
    62	## Main declarations
    63	
    64	* `CategoryTheory.GrpObj.pointTranslation` — the automorphism `(· * x⁻¹y)` of a group object,
    65	  carrying the point `x` to the point `y`.
    66	* `CategoryTheory.GrpObj.pointTranslationIso` — the same, as an isomorphism of the underlying
    67	  scheme of a group scheme `G : Over S`.
    68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_of_isIso` — the cotangent dimension is
    69	  invariant under an isomorphism of schemes.
    70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_of_pointTranslation` — the cotangent

1380	`PicScheme C`: the group structure `GrpObj (PicScheme C)` (by Yoneda
  1381	transport, `PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`) and local finiteness, carried by
  1382	`PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1)). Consequently
  1383	the §1 substrate theorems (`isOpenSubgroupScheme`,
  1384	`isSubgroupHomomorphism`, `identityComponent_geometricallyConnected`,
  1385	`baseChangeIso`) apply to `Pic⁰_{C/k}` definitionally. -/
  1386	noncomputable def Pic0Scheme {k : Type u} [Field k]
  1387	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
  1388	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  1389	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
  1390	    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :
  1391	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
  1392	  GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)
  1393	
  1394	/-! ## §3. The degree map
  1395	
  1396	The disjoint-union structure of `Pic_{C/k}` (a disjoint union of open
  1397	quasi-projective `k`-subschemes, indexed by Hilbert polynomial via
  1398	`PicScheme.smoothProperQuotient`) stratifies its `T`-points by the leading
  1399	coefficient of the Hilbert polynomial of a representing invertible sheaf
  1400	relative to a fixed degree-one polarisation. On `k`-points this gives the
  1401	**degree map** `Pic_{C/k}(k) → ℤ`.
  1402	
  1403	Blueprint reference: `def:divisor_degree_pic` (Milne III.1, p.~88). -/
  1404	
  1405	namespace PicScheme
  1406	
  1407	/-! ### The degree, factored through the relative Picard group
  1408	
  1409	The route below replaces the Quot/Hilbert-polynomial construction the section header
  1410	describes. Two facts make it work, and neither needs Quot:
  1411	
  1412	1. **Representability already does the transport.** `PicScheme.representable C` is a
  1413	   bijection `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` natural in `T`; taking
  1414	   `T = Spec k` (the trivial over-object `Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))`) sends a `k`-rational point
  1415	   of `Pic_{C/k}` to a relative Picard class over the base. This is `classOfSection` below,
  1416	   and it is sorry-free.
  1417	2. **The degree is a homomorphism on those classes.** ⚠ This was described here as "the one
  1418	   remaining input, isolated as the class `ClassDegree`". That is **false** and is corrected at
  1419	   `ClassDegree` below: the class is inhabited by the zero homomorphism with no hypothesis, so
  1420	   it demands nothing and `degreeOfSection` is not pinned to the degree. What is actually
  1421	   missing is a *characterisation* of the homomorphism. The sibling project builds exactly this
  1422	   homomorphism sorry-free and without Quot — `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`,
  1423	   `RiemannRoch/RelPicDegree.lean`, `relPicDeg : Additive (relPic C (overSpec k K)) →+ ℤ`,
  1424	   descended from `classDeg` along the observation that `Spec K` is a one-point space so its
  1425	   Čech Picard group is trivial and cannot contribute. Its own input is the closed χ-ledger
  1426	   `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg D` (`RiemannRoch/ChiLedger.lean`), whose 22-file / 5.5k-line
  1427	   closure I measured to be free of `sorry`.
  1428	
  1429	WHY `degree`'s DOMAIN IS AWKWARD — but *not* a reason it cannot be defined. `degree` takes an
  1430	*arbitrary* morphism `Spec k ⟶ (PicScheme C).left`, not a morphism over `Spec k`. Such a
  1431	morphism need not be a section of `(PicScheme C).hom` — the goal
  1432	`lambda ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙 (Spec k)` is not derivable — so it does not name a
  1433	`k`-*rational* point and representability says nothing about it.
  1434	
  1435	⚠ AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS PARAGRAPH DREW A FALSE CONCLUSION from that, and it is corrected
  1436	at `degree` (now closed, run 0067 r4) rather than only here. It read: "A total function of that
  1437	type therefore cannot be built from the Picard functor at all; it would have to invent a value
  1438	off the sections." Inventing a value off the sections is precisely what a total function of
  1439	this type is *allowed* to do — `fun _ => 0` inhabits the type — so the impossibility claim was
  1440	false, and the observation only ever constrained which values are **pinned**. `degree` is now
  1441	defined by cases on the section condition, agreeing with `degreeOfSectionPinned` where that is
  1442	meaningful; see `degree_eq_degreeOfSectionPinned`.
  1443	
  1444	Consumers should still prefer `degreeOfSection` / `degreeOfSectionPinned`, which carry the
  1445	section hypothesis in their types and so cannot be misread as speaking about non-sections. -/
  1446	
  1447	/-- An additive integer-valued function on relative Picard classes of `C` over the base field
  1448	— the carrier shape of Milne III.1 p.~88.
  1449	
  1450	**⚠ THIS CLASS IS VACUOUS AS STATED, and the docstring that used to sit here — "the one
  1451	remaining input to the degree map" — was FALSE.** Corrected run 0067 r2 after inbox issue
  1452	I-0534, re-verified by machine rather than accepted on report:
  1453	
  1454	```
  1455	theorem probe_classDegree_no_gate … : PicScheme.ClassDegree C := ⟨⟨0⟩⟩
  1456	-- axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]   -- no gate, no sorry
  1457	```
  1458	
  1459	The field asks only for `Nonempty (… →+ ℤ)`, and the **zero homomorphism** inhabits that type
  1460	with no hypothesis whatsoever. So `ClassDegree` is a *theorem* of this project, not an open
  1461	input, and nothing here demands that the chosen map be a degree.
  1462	
  1463	WHAT THAT COSTS THE CONSUMERS BELOW, stated plainly: `degreeOfSection` is total but **not
  1464	pinned to the degree** — `degreeOfSection ≡ 0` is a permitted reading of every statement in this
  1465	section — and `degreeOfSection_eq_zero_of_class_eq_zero` is correspondingly contentless (it is
  1466	`map_zero`, true of the zero map too). Do not cite them as a constructed degree map.
  1467	
  1468	THE REAL MISSING INPUT is a **characterisation**, not an existence claim: agreement of the
  1469	chosen homomorphism with `Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree` on the class of `𝒪(D)`, or with the
  1470	sibling's `relPicDeg` under the carrier comparison. That is what would make the class
  1471	non-vacuous and the degree unique. The class is retained (rather than deleted) only because
  1472	`degreeOfSection` is pinned against it; whoever adds the pinning field owns updating both.
  1473	
  1474	Contrast the house pattern: `HasPicScheme` and `HasFiniteMapToP1` are well *stated* because they
  1475	assert existence of an object satisfying a *nontrivial property*, where this one asks for a map
  1476	with no property — which is why it collapsed. But note the difference between a good statement
  1477	and an inhabited one (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-29): `HasFiniteMapToP1` has a derived instance,
  1478	whereas `HasPicScheme` has **zero** instances — its only producer, `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`,
  1479	is deliberately not an instance and needs `[HasRationalPoint C]`, which itself has no
  1480	unconditional producer since `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` was deleted as FALSE (`I-0491`). So
  1481	`HasPicScheme` is the right shape over an empty domain, and 70 declarations bind it. New work
  1482	belongs on `HasPicSchemeEt`/`picEt`. -/
  1483	class ClassDegree {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
  1484	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  1485	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : Prop where
  1486	  /-- An additive degree on the relative Picard classes over the base. -/
  1487	  nonempty_classDegree : Nonempty
  1488	    ((PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj (Opposite.op (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))))) →+ ℤ)
  1489	
  1490	/-- **The pinned degree interface** — `ClassDegree` with the missing characterisation supplied,
  1491	so that the chosen homomorphism *is* a degree rather than an arbitrary map. (Run 0067 r3.)
  1492	
  1493	`ClassDegree` above asks only for `Nonempty (… →+ ℤ)` and is therefore inhabited by the zero
  1494	map with no hypothesis — machine-verified, see its docstring. This class is the repair, and
  1495	the pin is taken **against the Abel map**, which is the one degree-carrying structure this
  1496	project already owns sorry-free:
  1497	
  1498	* `classDegree` is the homomorphism (now *data*, not a `Nonempty`, so that consumers get the
  1499	  same map rather than a re-chosen one);
  1500	* `classDegree_abel` is the characterisation: on the class of `𝒪(D)` for a relative divisor
  1501	  family of constant fibre degree `d`, the value is `d`. `PicScheme.abelMap` is
  1502	  `abelMapWitness` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, sorry-free), and
  1503	  `DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg` is the constant-fibre-degree predicate of `Picard/DivDegree.lean`.
  1504	
  1505	WHY THIS PIN AND NOT THE `WeilDivisor.degree` ONE. Agreement with `Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree`
  1506	on `𝒪(D)` — the characterisation the previous docstring named — needs a divisor-to-line-bundle
  1507	comparison that this project does not have at the relative level; the Abel map *is* that
  1508	comparison, already built and already carrying the degree ledger
  1509	(`PicScheme.abelDeg_app_mk`, `DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.finrank_fiber_cokernel`). So the pin
  1510	is stated where the existing structure can discharge it.
  1511	
  1512	THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, run before landing this — the lesson of `ClassDegree`'s own collapse and
  1513	of the parallel `SymPowData` defect (inbox I-0493, 2026-07-28) is that a class must be probed

1	/-

     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.DegreeBaseFieldInvariance
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The degree on the relative Picard group over a field (gap G-D5(b), SB-5 descent gadgets)
    10	
    11	For the challenge curve `C : Over (Spec k)` and a field extension `K` of `k`, the relative
    12	Picard group `relPic C (overSpec k K) = CechPic(C_K) ⧸ picFromBase` quotients out the classes
    13	pulled back from `Spec K` — but `Spec K` is a one-point space, so its Čech Picard group is
    14	trivial (`Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`) and `classDeg K` kills `picFromBase`
    15	(`classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase`).  The degree therefore descends to the relative
    16	Picard group:
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicDeg K : Additive (relPic C (overSpec k K)) →+ ℤ`, with the anchor
    19	  `relPicDeg_relPicMk : relPicDeg K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) L) = classDeg K L`;
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap` — **E-iv-alg descended to `relPic`**: the
    21	  relative degree is invariant under restriction along `Spec` of any `k`-algebra map of
    22	  field extensions, `relPicDeg K₂ (relPicAlgMap C φ x) = relPicDeg K₁ x`.
    23	
    24	These are the two descent gadgets of `informal/deg-d5b-worksheet.md` §4 SB-5; the `degAt`
    25	brick (SB-6) consumes `relPicDeg` and `relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap` verbatim — on a field
    26	representative `(K', y)` of an étale-locally-trivial class, the honest degree is
    27	`relPicDeg K' y`, well-defined across representatives by `relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap`.
    28	-/
    29	
    30	set_option autoImplicit false
    31	
    32	universe u
    33	
    34	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    35	
    36	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    37	
    38	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    39	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    40	
    41	/-! ## `classDeg` kills the classes from the base -/
    42	
    43	/-- **The degree vanishes on classes pulled back from the base field**: `Spec K` is a
    44	one-point space, so its Čech Picard group is trivial and every class of `picFromBase` is
    45	trivial. -/
    46	theorem classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    47	    {L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic} (hL : L ∈ picFromBase C (overSpec k K)) :
    48	    classDeg K L = 0 := by
    49	  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := (mem_picFromBase_iff C).mp hL
    50	  haveI : Subsingleton (overSpec k K).left :=
    51	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
    52	  rw [Scheme.CechPic.eq_one_of_subsingleton (overSpec k K).left N, map_one, classDeg_one]
    53	
    54	/-! ## The relative degree -/
    55	
    56	/-- **The degree on the relative Picard group over a field** (worksheet SB-5, first descent
    57	gadget): `classDeg K` descends along `relPicMk` to the quotient
    58	`relPic C (overSpec k K) = CechPic(C_K) ⧸ picFromBase`, because the Čech Picard group of the
    59	one-point scheme `Spec K` is trivial.  The `degAt` brick (SB-6) reads the degree of a
    60	field-representative of an étale-locally-trivial class through this homomorphism. -/
    61	noncomputable def relPicDeg (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    62	    Additive (relPic C (overSpec k K)) →+ ℤ :=
    63	  MonoidHom.toAdditiveLeft
    64	    (QuotientGroup.lift (picFromBase C (overSpec k K))
    65	      (AddMonoidHom.toMultiplicativeRight (classDeg K))
    66	      (fun L hL => by
    67	        have h0 : classDeg K L = 0 := classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase hL
    68	        rw [MonoidHom.mem_ker]
    69	        change Multiplicative.ofAdd (classDeg K L) = 1
    70	        rw [h0, ofAdd_zero]))
    71	
    72	/-- **The anchor of the relative degree**: on the class of `L`, the relative degree is
    73	`classDeg K L`. -/
    74	@[simp]
    75	theorem relPicDeg_relPicMk (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    76	    (L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic) :
    77	    relPicDeg K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) L) = classDeg K L :=
    78	  rfl
    79	
    80	/-- **E-iv-alg descended to the relative Picard group** (worksheet SB-5, second descent
    81	gadget): the relative degree is invariant under restriction along `Spec` of a `k`-algebra
    82	map `φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂` of field extensions — the degree of a relative Picard class does not
    83	depend on the field over which it is presented. -/
    84	theorem relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap {K₁ K₂ : Type u} [Field K₁] [Algebra k K₁] [Field K₂]
    85	    [Algebra k K₂] (φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂) (x : relPic C (overSpec k K₁)) :
    86	    relPicDeg K₂ (relPicAlgMap C φ x) = relPicDeg K₁ x := by
    87	  induction x using relPic.ind with
    88	  | mk L =>
    89	    have h1 : relPicAlgMap C φ (relPicMk C (overSpec k K₁) L)
    90	        = relPicMk C (overSpec k K₂)
    91	          (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left) L) :=
    92	      relPicMap_mk C (Over.overSpecMap φ) L
    93	    rw [h1, relPicDeg_relPicMk, relPicDeg_relPicMk,
    94	      classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition C φ L]
    95	
    96	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicAlgebra
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.EtaleCover
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The étale plus construction of the relative Picard functor on affine tests
    11	
    12	For a curve `C` over `k` and an affine test scheme `Spec A`, the étale-sheafified relative
    13	Picard group is computed by a *single* plus construction (the relative Picard presheaf is
    14	étale-separated, by descent — proved separately): a class of the plus is represented by a
    15	relative Picard class on an étale cover `Spec B → Spec A` equipped with a *descent
    16	condition* — equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double cover
    17	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` — and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common
    18	refinement.
    19	
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentClasses C E`: the subgroup of `relPic C (Spec B)` of classes
    21	  satisfying the descent condition on the cover `E` with carrier `B`.
    22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap C h`: transport of descent classes along a refinement map
    23	  `h` of covers.
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_congr` (**the keystone**): a descent class restricts
    25	  equally along any two `A`-algebra maps out of the cover carrier — the pair `(j₁, j₂)`
    26	  factors through the double cover, where the descent condition kills the difference.
    27	  Specialized to refinement maps as `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap_congr`, this is what
    28	  makes the colimit below independent of all choices; applied across base rings
    29	  (`Picard/PicEtAffMap.lean`), it is also what makes the plus functorial in the test
    30	  algebra.
    31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff C A`: the one-step plus — descent classes on some cover,
    32	  modulo agreement on a common refinement — with its `CommGroup` structure and the
    33	  constructor/eliminator API `PicEtAff.mk`, `PicEtAff.ind`, `PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff`,
    34	  `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap`.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit`: the unit `relPic C (Spec A) →* PicEtAff C A` of the
    36	  plus construction — a class pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological
    37	  descent datum.
    38	
    39	The functoriality of `PicEtAff` in `A` (restriction along test maps, via base change of
    40	covers) and the comparison theorems (injectivity of the unit = separatedness; bijectivity
    41	under a section = rigidification) are subsequent layers, consuming only this interface.
    42	-/
    43	
    44	set_option autoImplicit false
    45	
    46	universe u
    47	
    48	open CategoryTheory
    49	
    50	open scoped TensorProduct
    51	
    52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    53	
    54	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    55	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    56	
    57	noncomputable section
    58	
    59	/-! ## Descent classes on an étale cover -/
    60	
    61	/-- The first coprojection from the carrier of a cover into its self-tensor product over
    62	the base — the algebra face of the first projection of the double cover
    63	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B) → Spec B` — as a `k`-algebra map. -/
    64	def doubleInl (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
    65	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
    66	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
    67	
    68	/-- The second coprojection into the self-tensor product; see `doubleInl`. -/
    69	def doubleInr (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
    70	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
    71	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight).restrictScalars k
    72	
    73	/-- The subgroup of relative Picard classes on an étale cover of the test algebra
    74	satisfying the descent condition: equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double
    75	cover. -/
    76	def descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
    77	    Subgroup (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
    78	  MonoidHom.eqLocus
    79	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E))
    80	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E))
    81	
    82	lemma mem_descentClasses_iff {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
    83	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} :
    84	    x ∈ descentClasses C E ↔
    85	      relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
    86	        = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x :=
    87	  Iff.rfl
    88	
    89	/-! ## Transport along refinement maps -/
    90	
    91	private lemma doubleInl_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
    92	    (doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
    93	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) := by
    94	  ext x
    95	  simp [doubleInl]
    96	
    97	private lemma doubleInr_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
    98	    (doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
    99	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) := by
   100	  ext x
   101	  simp [doubleInr]
   102	
   103	/-- The descent condition is natural in the cover: pullback along a refinement map sends
   104	descent classes to descent classes. -/
   105	lemma relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
   106	    (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)}
   107	    (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
   108	    relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x ∈ descentClasses C F := by
   109	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff] at hx ⊢
   110	  calc relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x)
   111	      = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x :=
   112	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
   113	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
   114	          (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [doubleInl_comp h]
   115	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
   116	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) := relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
   117	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
   118	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by rw [hx]
   119	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
   120	          (doubleInr E)) x := (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
   121	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x := by
   122	        rw [doubleInr_comp h]
   123	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x) :=
   124	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
   125	
   126	/-- Transport of descent classes along a refinement map of covers. -/
   127	def descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
   128	    descentClasses C E →* descentClasses C F :=
   129	  ((relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k)).comp (descentClasses C E).subtype).codRestrict _
   130	    fun x => relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses C h x.2
   131	
   132	@[simp]
   133	lemma descentMap_coe {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
   134	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
   135	    (descentMap C h x : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
   136	      = relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
   137	  rfl
   138	
   139	@[simp]
   140	lemma descentMap_id {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (x : descentClasses C E) :
   141	    descentMap C (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier) x = x := by
   142	  ext
   143	  rw [descentMap_coe,
   144	    show (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k = AlgHom.id k E.Carrier from rfl]
   145	  exact relPicAlgMap_id C _
   146	
   147	lemma descentMap_comp {E F G : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
   148	    (h' : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
   149	    descentMap C (h'.comp h) x = descentMap C h' (descentMap C h x) := by
   150	  ext
   151	  rw [descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe,
   152	    show (h'.comp h).restrictScalars k
   153	      = (h'.restrictScalars k).comp (h.restrictScalars k) from rfl]
   154	  exact relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
   155	
   156	/-- **Generalized refinement-map independence**, the keystone of the plus construction:
   157	a class satisfying the descent condition restricts equally along any two `A`-algebra maps
   158	out of the cover carrier — into an arbitrary test algebra, not merely another cover.  The
   159	pair `(j₁, j₂)` factors jointly through the double cover of the source, where the descent
   160	condition identifies the two pullbacks. -/
   161	theorem relPicAlgMap_congr {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
   162	    [Algebra k R] [Algebra A R] [IsScalarTower k A R] (j₁ j₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R)
   163	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
   164	    relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by
   165	  set H : E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R :=
   166	    Algebra.TensorProduct.lift j₁ j₂ fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _ with hH
   167	  have key₁ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) = j₁.restrictScalars k := by
   168	    ext y
   169	    simp [hH, doubleInl]
   170	  have key₂ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) = j₂.restrictScalars k := by
   171	    ext y
   172	    simp [hH, doubleInr]
   173	  calc relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x
   174	      = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [key₁]
   175	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) :=
   176	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
   177	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by
   178	        have hx' : relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
   179	            = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x := hx
   180	        rw [hx']
   181	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E)) x :=
   182	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _).symm
   183	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by rw [key₂]
   184	
   185	/-- **Refinement-map independence**: any two refinement maps between the same covers
   186	transport descent classes identically — what makes the plus construction independent of
   187	all choices. -/
   188	theorem descentMap_congr {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
   189	    (h₁ h₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
   190	    descentMap C h₁ x = descentMap C h₂ x :=
   191	  Subtype.ext (relPicAlgMap_congr C h₁ h₂ x.2)
   192	
   193	/-! ## The plus construction -/
   194	
   195	/-- Two descent-class representatives are identified when they agree after transport to a
   196	common refinement.  By `descentMap_congr` the choice of transport maps is immaterial, so
   197	the relation is an equivalence (directedness of covers gives transitivity). -/
   198	instance picEtAffSetoid : Setoid (Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) where
   199	  r p q := ∃ (F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : p.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
   200	    (g : q.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier), descentMap C f p.2 = descentMap C g q.2
   201	  iseqv := by
   202	    constructor
   203	    · exact fun p => ⟨p.1, AlgHom.id A _, AlgHom.id A _, rfl⟩
   204	    · rintro p q ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩
   205	      exact ⟨F, g, f, hfg.symm⟩
   206	    · rintro p q r ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩ ⟨G, f', g', hfg'⟩
   207	      refine ⟨F.prod G, (F.prodInl G).comp f, (F.prodInr G).comp g', ?_⟩
   208	      rw [descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp, hfg, ← descentMap_comp, ← descentMap_comp,
   209	        descentMap_congr C ((F.prodInl G).comp g) ((F.prodInr G).comp f') q.2,
   210	        descentMap_comp, hfg', ← descentMap_comp]
   211	
   212	variable (A) in
   213	/-- The one-step étale plus of the relative Picard functor at the affine test `Spec A`:
   214	relative Picard classes on some presented étale cover satisfying the descent condition,
   215	modulo agreement on a common refinement.  On affine tests this *is* the étale
   216	sheafification of the relative Picard presheaf (one plus suffices because the presheaf is
   217	étale-separated — proved separately). -/
   218	def PicEtAff : Type u :=
   219	  Quotient (picEtAffSetoid C (A := A))
   220	
   221	namespace PicEtAff
   222	
   223	/-- The plus class of a relative Picard class with a descent condition on a cover. -/
   224	def mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) : PicEtAff C A :=
   225	  Quotient.mk _ ⟨E, x⟩
   226	
   227	@[elab_as_elim]
   228	theorem ind {motive : PicEtAff C A → Prop}
   229	    (mk : ∀ (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E), motive (mk C E x)) :
   230	    ∀ q, motive q := by
   231	  intro q
   232	  induction q using Quotient.ind with
   233	  | _ p => exact mk p.1 p.2
   234	
   235	theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {x : descentClasses C E}
   236	    {y : descentClasses C F} :
   237	    mk C E x = mk C F y ↔
   238	      ∃ (G : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier)
   239	        (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier), descentMap C f x = descentMap C g y :=
   240	  Quotient.eq
   241	
   242	/-- Transporting the representative to a finer cover does not change the plus class. -/
   243	@[simp]
   244	theorem mk_descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
   245	    (x : descentClasses C E) : mk C F (descentMap C h x) = mk C E x :=
   246	  Quotient.sound ⟨F, AlgHom.id A F.Carrier, h, by rw [descentMap_id]⟩
   247	
   248	/-! ### The group structure -/
   249	
   250	/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the left factor. -/
   251	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inl {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
   252	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
   253	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
   254	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x)
   255	      = descentMap C f x := by
   256	  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInl]
   257	
   258	/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the right factor. -/
   259	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inr {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
   260	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
   261	    (y : descentClasses C F) :
   262	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y)

    10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
    11	
    12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
    13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
    14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
    15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
    16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
    19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
    21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
    22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
    23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
    25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
    27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
    28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
    29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
    30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
    31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
    32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
    33	-/
    34	
    35	set_option autoImplicit false
    36	
    37	universe u
    38	
    39	open CategoryTheory
    40	
    41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    42	
    43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    45	
    46	noncomputable section

    48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
    49	
    50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
    51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
    52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
    53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
    54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
    56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    57	
    58	section DegAt
    59	
    60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    61	
    62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
    63	@[simp]
    64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
    65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
    66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
    67	
    68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
    69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
    71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
    72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
    74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
    75	
    76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
    77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
    79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
    80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
    81	  rfl
    82	
    83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
    84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
    85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
    86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
    87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
    89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
    90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
    91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
    92	
    93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
    94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
    97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
    98	
    99	end DegAt

   101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
   102	
   103	variable (C) in
   104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
   105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
   106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
   107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
   108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   109	    degAt lam t = 0}
   110	  one_mem' := by
   111	    intro K _ _ t
   112	    exact degAt_one t
   113	  mul_mem' := by
   114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
   115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
   116	  inv_mem' := by
   117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
   118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
   119	
   120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
   121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
   122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
   123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
   125	  Iff.rfl
   126	
   127	variable (C) in
   128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
   129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
   130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
   131	points. -/
   132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
   133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
   134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
   135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
   136	
   137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
   138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
   139	@[simp]
   140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
   141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
   142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
   143	  rfl
   144	
   145	variable (C) in
   146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
   147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
   148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
   149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
   150	functor. -/
   151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
   152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
   153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
   154	  map_id T := by
   155	    ext lam U
   156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
   157	  map_comp g h := by
   158	    ext lam U
   159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
   160	
   161	@[simp]
   162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
   163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
   164	  rfl
   165	
   166	@[simp]
   167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
   168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
   169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
   170	  rfl
   171	
   172	variable (C) in
   173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
   174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
   175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/
   176	def pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
   177	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype
   178	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl
   179	
   180	end

    10	
    11	The usable form of the (C1) étale-separatedness theorem
    12	(`AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit_injective`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechKernelLemma`)
    13	for the Layer-2 gluing arguments: for a curve `C` (proper, geometrically irreducible and
    14	geometrically reduced over `k`), a `k`-algebra `R` and a presented étale cover `E` of
    15	`Spec R`, two relative Picard classes over `R` with equal restrictions to the cover
    16	carrier are equal (`AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_injective_of_etaleCover`).
    17	
    18	Indeed, the unit of the plus construction sends a class `z` to its tautological descent
    19	class represented on *any* cover (`PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk`), so equal restrictions give
    20	equal units, and the unit is injective by (C1).
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    32	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    33	
    34	/-- The composite `R → Γ(self cover) → Γ(E)` of the tautological identifications is the
    35	structure map of the carrier of `E`. -/
    36	private lemma fromSelf_comp_ofId (E : Algebra.EtaleCover R) :
    37	    (E.fromSelf.restrictScalars k).comp
    38	        ((Algebra.ofId R (Algebra.EtaleCover.self R).Carrier).restrictScalars k)
    39	      = (Algebra.ofId R E.Carrier).restrictScalars k := by
    40	  ext r
    41	  simp only [AlgHom.coe_comp, AlgHom.coe_restrictScalars', Function.comp_apply,
    42	    Algebra.ofId_apply, Algebra.EtaleCover.fromSelf, AlgHom.coe_comp]
    43	  exact congrArg (algebraMap R E.Carrier)
    44	    (((Algebra.EtaleCover.selfEquiv R).commutes r).trans rfl)
    45	
    46	/-- The unit of the plus construction, represented on an arbitrary cover: `unit z` is the
    47	class of the tautological descent datum of `z` on any presented étale cover `E`. -/
    48	theorem PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover R) (z : relPic C (overSpec k R)) :
    49	    PicEtAff.unit C R z
    50	      = PicEtAff.mk C E
    51	          ⟨relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId R E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
    52	            tautological_mem_descentClasses C E z⟩ := by
    53	  have hval : descentMap C E.fromSelf
    54	        ⟨relPicAlgMap C
    55	            ((Algebra.ofId R (Algebra.EtaleCover.self R).Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
    56	          tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self R) z⟩
    57	      = ⟨relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId R E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
    58	          tautological_mem_descentClasses C E z⟩ := by
    59	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
    60	    rw [descentMap_coe, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, fromSelf_comp_ofId]
    61	  calc PicEtAff.unit C R z
    62	      = PicEtAff.mk C (.self R)
    63	          ⟨relPicAlgMap C
    64	              ((Algebra.ofId R (Algebra.EtaleCover.self R).Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
    65	            tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self R) z⟩ := rfl
    66	    _ = PicEtAff.mk C E (descentMap C E.fromSelf
    67	          ⟨relPicAlgMap C
    68	              ((Algebra.ofId R (Algebra.EtaleCover.self R).Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
    69	            tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self R) z⟩) :=
    70	        (PicEtAff.mk_descentMap C E.fromSelf _).symm
    71	    _ = PicEtAff.mk C E
    72	          ⟨relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId R E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
    73	            tautological_mem_descentClasses C E z⟩ := by rw [hval]
    74	
    75	variable [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
    76	
    77	/-- **Restriction of relative Picard classes to an étale cover is injective** — the
    78	consumable corollary of the (C1) étale-separatedness theorem: two relative Picard
    79	classes over `R` agreeing on a presented étale cover of `Spec R` agree.  This is what
    80	licenses every gluing step of the Layer-2 functor. -/
    81	theorem relPicAlgMap_injective_of_etaleCover (E : Algebra.EtaleCover R) :
    82	    Function.Injective
    83	      (relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId R E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) := by
    84	  intro x y h
    85	  apply PicEtAff.unit_injective C R
    86	  rw [PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C E x, PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C E y]
    87	  exact congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C E) (Subtype.ext h)
    88	
    89	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# The identity component of the Picard scheme

Let `G` be a `k`-group scheme locally of finite type. Its **identity
component** `G⁰` is the connected component of `|G|` containing the image of
the identity section. It is an open and closed subgroup scheme of `G`, of
finite type and geometrically irreducible over `k`, and its formation
commutes with extension of the base field (Kleiman, §5, Lem.~`lem:agps`).

This file develops that substrate for an arbitrary `k`-group scheme (§1) and
then specialises it to `G = Pic_{C/k}`, the Picard scheme of a smooth proper
geometrically integral curve `C/k` (§2), obtaining `Pic⁰_{C/k}` together with
the degree map `Pic_{C/k}(k) → ℤ` (§3) whose kernel it cuts out on
`k`-points (§4). For `C` of positive genus, `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is the Jacobian
variety of `C`.

## Main results

- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` — the identity component

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0Dimension

/-!
# Homogeneity of a group scheme: translations, and the invariants they move

A group scheme is **homogeneous**: any point can be carried to any other by an automorphism
of the underlying scheme, namely a translation. This file supplies the translation and the
consequence the dimension chapter needs — that a *pointwise* invariant of the local rings is
constant along the orbit of the translations, so a bound at one point is a bound at every
point in that orbit.

## Why this file exists

`Picard/Pic0Dimension.lean` reduces `dim Pic⁰_{C/k} = g(C)` to two halves. The `≥` half
needs the cotangent dimension at the **identity** only, and is front (a) of this chapter.

/-! ## §1. Zariski-local presheaves on `Sch/S` (moved from
`GrassmannianRepresentability.lean`) -/

/-- The restriction of `T : Over S` to an open `W ⊆ T.left`, as an object of
`Over S`. -/
noncomputable def overRes {S : Scheme.{0}} (T : Over S) (W : T.left.Opens) :
    Over S :=
  Over.mk (W.ι ≫ T.hom)

/-- The restriction morphism `T|_W ⟶ T` in `Over S`. -/
noncomputable def overResHom {S : Scheme.{0}} (T : Over S) (W : T.left.Opens) :
    overRes T W ⟶ T :=
  Over.homMk W.ι rfl

/-- The inclusion `T|_{W'} ⟶ T|_W` in `Over S` attached to `W' ≤ W`. -/
noncomputable def overResLE {S : Scheme.{0}} (T : Over S)
    {W' W : T.left.Opens} (h : W' ≤ W) : overRes T W' ⟶ overRes T W :=
  Over.homMk (T.left.homOfLE h)
    ((Category.assoc _ _ _).symm.trans
      (congrArg (· ≫ T.hom) (T.left.homOfLE_ι h)))
